name: Benga
desc: Kenya's iconic national guitar style characterized by bright, rolling lead guitar riffs, interlocking basslines, and syncopated high-hat rhythms.

name: Gengetone
desc: The raw youth movement birthed in 2018 featuring rapid-fire Sheng bars, bouncing 808 kicks, and infectious street anthems.

name: Urbantone
desc: The modern evolution of Kenyan street sound, fusing classic Kapuka/Genge nostalgia with amapiano log drums and laid-back Sheng flows.

name: Genge
desc: The foundational Kenyan hip-hop sound pioneered by Calif Records in early 2000s, telling conversational everyday street stories.

name: Kapuka
desc: The signature Ogopa Deejays boom of the 2000s that dominated East African dancefloors with infectious synthesizer hooks and call-and-response choruses.

name: Afropop
desc: Vibrant, radio-friendly contemporary African pop blending Afrobeat grooves with rich Swahili melodic hooks.

name: Taarab
desc: Centuries-old coastal Swahili musical poetry featuring classical oud, violins, qanun, and heartfelt love and philosophical verses.

name: Afrofusion
desc: Sophisticated blend of indigenous Kenyan folk rhythms with contemporary jazz, neo-soul, funk, and acoustic vocal arrangements.

name: Swahili pop
desc: Smooth coastal R&B and Bongo-adjacent melodies celebrating romance, coastal warmth, and Swahili poetic elegance.

name: Hip hop
desc: Hard-hitting lyrical storytelling, classic boom-bap, and trap beats chronicling urban realities and political consciousness.

name: Reggae/dancehall
desc: Deep roots reggae and vibrant dancehall deeply entrenched in Kenyan matatu sound system culture and youth expression.

name: Benga fusion
desc: Innovative fusion of traditional Benga lead guitar fingerpicking with modern electronic synths, trap hi-hats, and pop vocals.

name: Rhumba
desc: Sensuous brass arrangements, sebene dance climaxes, and timeless guitar arpeggios that have captivated Kenyan generations.

name: Ohangla
desc: Hypnotic high-tempo traditional Luo dance music driven by the orutu single-string fiddle, electric bass, and rapid talking drums.

name: Mugithi
desc: Acoustic one-man guitar folk music, country picking, and communal call-and-response train dance anthems popular across Central Kenya.

name: Isikuti
desc: UNESCO-recognized celebratory indigenous dance tradition powered by a set of three resonant Isukuti drums, bells, and communal horn calls.
